Adding and editing species occurrence data

Source: vignettes/upload-edit-species-occurrence.Rmd
upload-edit-species-occurrence.Rmd

Overview

nwrspeciesr provides experimental functions for adding and editing species occurrence records through the authenticated SpeciesUpload API. This article uses Tetlin National Wildlife Refuge to demonstrate a cautious workflow:

  1. load an API key without placing it in a script;
  2. identify refuges writable by the key;
  3. create a test occurrence record;
  4. capture the returned speciesId;
  5. add evidence to the created record; and
  6. replace one or more records when a full replacement is appropriate.

These operations modify staging data. Run them only with an API key intended for the staging service, and use a test record and test evidence URL. The examples are not evaluated while the package website is built.

Write operations are not reversible

The upload functions can create or modify NWRSpecies records. Confirm the refuge, taxon, payload, and permissions before sending each request. Never put an API key directly in a script, README, or version-controlled file.

Configure the API key

The upload functions read NWRSPECIES_API_KEY when api_key = NULL. Store the key in a user-level .Renviron file and restart R before using it:

# Check only whether the key is available; do not print the key.
nzchar(Sys.getenv("NWRSPECIES_API_KEY", unset = ""))

The upload API defaults to the staging endpoint:

https://staging-iris.fws.gov/APPS/SpeciesAPI/api/

The package does not expose the API key in returned objects or error messages.

Check upload permissions

Start by asking the API which refuge units the key can modify:

library(nwrspeciesr)

permissions <- get_upload_permissions()
permissions

Do not assume that a key can edit every refuge. A successful permissions request only establishes which refuge units are writable; it does not authorize every species record or every operation.

Find the Tetlin entry in the returned table and use its refugeCode. Inspect column names first because the service response can change:

names(permissions)

For example, after confirming the Tetlin row in the printed permissions table, assign its code explicitly:

tetlin_code <- "FF07RTET00"

If Tetlin is not listed in permissions, stop here. The API key must be authorized for Tetlin before creating or editing records there. Do not use a code copied from another refuge or guess a code from a name.

Create a test occurrence record

A new record requires refugeCode and taxonCode. The remaining creation fields receive documented API defaults. The example uses a taxon code only as a demonstration; replace it with the approved ITIS TSN for the species in your test record.

created <- create_species_record(
  list(
    refugeCode = tetlin_code,
    taxonCode = 93710
  )
)

created
created$speciesId

The returned speciesId identifies the created record. Save it for subsequent operations rather than using an arbitrary ID from another environment:

test_species_id <- created$speciesId

New records default to a draft status and to conservative control values. Check the response before proceeding.

Add evidence to the test record

add_species_evidence() adds URL-based evidence to an existing record. Identify the record with speciesId, provide an ISO-formatted observation date, provide a date precision ID from the API documentation, and set at least one evidence type to TRUE.

evidence_result <- add_species_evidence(
  list(
    speciesId = test_species_id,
    url = "https://example.gov/report/123",
    observationDate = "2026-05-14",
    datePrecisionId = 1,
    photograph = TRUE
  )
)

evidence_result

Use a real, stable, publicly accessible evidence URL appropriate for the record. The example URL is only a placeholder and may not be suitable evidence for an actual record.

Replace one record

replace_species_record() performs a full replacement of one existing record. It is not a partial update. Include every field that should remain on the record, including the required control fields status, refugeAccepted, and isSensitive.

Before replacing a record, obtain or construct the complete intended payload. Do not send a list containing only the field you want to change.

replacement <- list(
  refugeCode = tetlin_code,
  taxonCode = 93710,
  status = "Draft",
  refugeAccepted = "Undecided",
  isSensitive = "No",
  occurrence = "Present",
  occurrenceNote = "Test record for staging workflow"
)

replaced <- replace_species_record(replacement)
replaced

The replacement payload must follow the API’s allowed fields and values. In a production workflow, preserve all existing fields that should remain before sending the replacement.

Replace multiple records in a batch

replace_species_records() is different from replace_species_record(): it sends multiple full replacement records in one all-or-nothing batch request. It accepts at most 25 records.

batch_replacements <- list(
  list(
    refugeCode = tetlin_code,
    taxonCode = 93710,
    status = "Draft",
    refugeAccepted = "Undecided",
    isSensitive = "No",
    occurrence = "Present"
  ),
  list(
    refugeCode = tetlin_code,
    taxonCode = 93711,
    status = "Draft",
    refugeAccepted = "Undecided",
    isSensitive = "No",
    occurrence = "Probably Present"
  )
)

replace_species_records(batch_replacements)

Use replace_species_record() for one record and replace_species_records() when several records should be replaced together. Because the batch request is all-or-nothing, validate every record before submitting the batch.

Create multiple records

For comparison, create_species_records() creates new records in one batch request and accepts up to 200 records. It does not replace existing records.

create_species_records(list(
  list(refugeCode = tetlin_code, taxonCode = 93710),
  list(refugeCode = tetlin_code, taxonCode = 93711)
))

Use creation functions for new records and replacement functions for existing records. Do not use a creation function to try to edit a record.

Troubleshooting authorization errors

The HTTP status helps distinguish common problems:

Status Interpretation
400 The request reached the API but failed validation. Inspect error$response_body for the invalid or missing field.
401 The API key was missing or not accepted.
403 The key was accepted but is not authorized for the requested refuge, record, or operation.
404 The endpoint or base URL is incorrect.

To inspect the API validation response without exposing the key:

tryCatch(
  create_species_record(
    list(refugeCode = tetlin_code, taxonCode = 93710)
  ),
  error = function(error) {
    error$response_body
  }
)

Do not include the API key or full authenticated request object when reporting an error.

Reproducibility and cleanup

Record the package version, staging endpoint, refuge code, taxon code, and request date for each test. Keep test records identifiable as staging tests and follow your local process for cleanup or review after testing.

list(
  retrieved = format(Sys.time(), tz = "UTC"),
  package_version = as.character(utils::packageVersion("nwrspeciesr")),
  refuge_code = tetlin_code,
  taxon_code = 93710
)
